title: Conditional rendering, lists and keys
summary: if, ternaries, && and early returns; rendering arrays with map; what keys are for, why index keys break reordering, and using keys to reset state.

sections.title: Choosing what to render
sections.body:
Use plain JavaScript. An early `return` or an `if` that assigns to a variable works for big branches; a ternary `cond ? <A /> : <B />` works inline; `cond && <A />` renders A or nothing. Return `null` to render nothing at all.

Make sure the left side of `&&` is a boolean. `0`, `NaN` and `""` are falsy but `0` and `NaN` are rendered as text (an empty string renders nothing).

sections.title: Lists with map
sections.body:
Render arrays with `map` and give each item a stable `key`: `items.map(item => <Row key={item.id} item={item} />)`. Filter and sort **before** mapping, using copies (`toSorted`, `filter`) so you never mutate props or state.

Keys must be unique **among siblings** only, not globally, and must be stable across renders. Put the key on the outermost element returned by the `map` callback; use `<Fragment key={…}>` if you return several elements.

sections.title: Why keys matter
sections.body:
React matches the children of one render to the next by key (or by position when there are no keys). With a stable id, React moves the existing DOM node and its **state** along with the item. With the **array index** as key, inserting at the top or reordering means index 0 is now a different item but keeps item 0's state, so inputs, checkboxes and animations attach to the wrong row.

Index keys are acceptable only for static lists that never reorder, insert or delete. `key={Math.random()}` is worse: every render creates new keys, so every row remounts and loses state and focus.

sections.title: Keys reset state
sections.body: A key change tells React "this is a different thing", so it unmounts the old component and mounts a fresh one with new state. This is the clean way to reset a form when the selected record changes: `<EditForm key={user.id} user={user} />`, instead of an effect that copies props into state.

pitfalls: Index keys on lists that reorder, filter or insert.
Generating keys with `Math.random()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` during render.
Putting the key on an inner element instead of the element returned by `map`.

gotchas.question: Do keys need to be unique across the whole page?
gotchas.answer: No. They must be unique among siblings in the same array. Two different lists can reuse the same ids.

gotchas.question: What happens to a typed-in input when you prepend an item to a list keyed by index?
gotchas.answer: The typed text stays at index 0, which now shows the new item, so the text appears on the wrong row. React reuses the component at each key, and index keys shift meaning.

gotchas.question: How do you reset all state in `<Profile user={user} />` when `user` changes?
gotchas.answer: Give it a key: `<Profile key={user.id} user={user} />`. A new key mounts a new instance with fresh state.
